name: Notifications
plain: Asks to show system notifications outside the browser tab.
meaning: Lets a site put messages on the person's desktop or lock screen. Reaches the person after they leave the page; abuse is spam, scams and fake alerts, so browsers add quiet prompts and auto-revocation.

access.prompt_ui: Chrome: bubble with Allow or Block, or a quiet address-bar chip (Notifications blocked) from Chrome 80 for sites people rarely allow. Firefox: Allow or Not now plus Always block, needs a gesture since 72. Safari: system sheet, needs a gesture.
access.persistence: Persistent per origin; Chrome auto-revokes unused or abusive sites and tells the person; Safari ties to the Notification Center
access.revocation: Padlock, Site settings, OS notification settings, Safety Hub one-tap unsubscribe on Android; Permissions API 'change' event.
access.iframe: Cross-origin iframes cannot request it; the requesting document must be top-level or same-origin with a gesture
steps: Call Notification.requestPermission() from a click (required in Firefox and Safari)
Browser shows prompt or quiet chip
Permission becomes granted, denied or stays default
Show with showNotification() or new Notification()

ios_safari.note: Home Screen web apps only, requires iOS 16.4

chrome_android.note: Constructor throws on Android, use showNotification

data.metric: Notification display with title, body, icon, actions
data.update: on demand, no rate limit besides OS

fields.name: actions
fields.range: up to Notification.maxActions (2 in Chrome desktop, 3 Android)

fields.name: tag, renotify
fields.range: replace earlier notification with same tag

limits.headline: Can show messages on your screen outside the browser tab, once you tap Allow
limits.user_action: You tap Allow on the site's notification pop up
can: Show alerts on your desktop or lock screen after you leave the page
Send chat, delivery or calendar updates you asked for
Keep sending until you block it in site settings
cannot: Show anything before you tap Allow
Keep showing alerts if you block the site or the browser auto removes it
Use a loud pop up if Chrome decides to show a quiet icon instead
Ask on iPhone unless the site is installed to the Home Screen
limits.differs: Chrome and Firefox ask in the browser. On iPhone, the site must be installed to the Home Screen. Chrome may show a quiet chip for sites people rarely allow.

story.what_it_is: A site asks to show pop up alerts on your device, even when you are not on the page.

marketing.name: Notification permission changes
marketing.pitch: Chrome moves unwanted notification requests to a quiet prompt, so pages ask less and you see fewer spam alerts.

story.for_you: A prompt asks if the site can send you notifications. If you allow, alerts appear on screen like app alerts. You can turn them off later in site settings.
story.for_makers: Makers use alerts to bring people back for news, messages, deals and live events. They are one of the strongest tools for return visits. Abuse is common, so browsers now quiet the prompts.

use_cases.example: A news site asks to alert you about breaking stories, which can pull you back several times a day.
A web chat shows a pop up when a friend replies while you are in another tab.
A browser game says your build has finished or a friend joined your game lobby.
A store alerts you about a price drop on a saved item or a delivery update.
A sports site sends goal alerts during a live match.
A calendar or task site alerts you before a meeting or due date.
Some sites use alerts as an ad channel, sending promotions for a fee from advertisers.
A bank sends a sign in alert when a new device logs in.

technical_bounds: No notification display when the OS denies Do Not Disturb or the browser is closed (service worker needed for push)
Cannot request without gesture on Firefox and Safari
iOS only for installed Home Screen web apps

history.change: Prompt requires a user gesture and shows quiet UI
Quieter notification UI for low-allow sites and abusive prompts
Web Push and notifications on macOS 13 (Safari 16.1 in Ventura)
Notifications for Home Screen web apps
